title: There's a bearish wrinkle in the market's hottest trade
excerpt: "The disinflationary effects of AI that Chair Warsh has been touting will have to wait a little longer," says Bank of America.
content_html:
By William Edwards

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Economists and central bankers like to extoll the disinflationary benefits of AI.

The new technology can help businesses produce more at lower costs. It can replace some human labor, meaning savings on wages. So, higher productivity and lower costs, combined with less wage-driven demand, lead to lower consumer prices.

While that may be all well and true in the long run, there's no doubt that AI — specifically, the cost of building out its infrastructure — is actually creating higher consumer prices now.

Look no further than July's CPI report, released Wednesday: computer prices rose 3.5% in a single month, while software prices climbed about 40% over the past year. Add in the rising cost of energy as data centers compete for power, and businesses passing along AI installation costs to customers, and AI starts to look inflationary, Bank of America said in a client note on Thursday.

"AI is not only raising input costs for electronics, but also driving a positive wealth effect that is supporting consumer demand," Stephen Juneau, an economist at the bank, said in the note.

"The disinflationary effects of AI that Chair Warsh has been touting will have to wait a little longer."

That's concerning for stocks on two fronts: both short- and long-term interest rates.

On the short end of the yield curve, AI contributing to higher inflation is complicating interest rate policy. The higher inflation is, the more the Federal Reserve feels pressure to hike its overnight lending rate. That acts as a brake on economic activity, and can slow earnings growth — the lifeblood of the stock market.

Tom Essaye, the founder of Sevens Report Research, told me Thursday that while the AI buildout is unlikely to lead to a sustained bout of inflation, it does strengthen the case for a one-and-done rate hike at the Fed's September meeting.

On the second front, inflation tends to push up long-term bond yields as investors demand higher returns when they expect inflation to erode their money's value. The 10-year Treasury yield is now at 4.64%, up from 4.15% at the start of the year.

While there are many factors influencing long-term interest rates, elevated investment spending is helping lift bond yields, MRB Partners said in a client note on Thursday. The firm sees long-term yields rising further, which could mean trouble for stocks.

"Our bearish outlook for US Treasurys will eventually be problematic for US equities," Philip Colmar, a partner of global strategy at MRB Partners, said in the note. He added that every time 10-year yields have broken out meaningfully to the upside since 2020, "equities have experienced a sharp correction."

作者：William Edwards 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

经济学家和央行行长喜欢宣扬人工智能的抑制通胀的好处。

新技术可以帮助企业以更低的成本生产更多产品。 它可以替代一些人力，意味着节省工资。 因此，更高的生产率和更低的成本，加上工资驱动的需求减少，导致消费者价格下降。

虽然从长远来看这可能是正确的，但毫无疑问，人工智能——特别是建设其基础设施的成本——现在实际上正在创造更高的消费者价格。

周三发布的 7 月份 CPI 报告就足以说明这一点：电脑价格单月上涨 3.5%，而软件价格在过去一年里上涨了约 40%。 美国银行在周四的一份客户报告中表示，随着数据中心争夺电力，加上企业将人工智能安装成本转嫁给客户，能源成本不断上升，人工智能开始看起来通胀。

该银行经济学家史蒂芬·朱诺（Stephen Juneau）在报告中表示：“人工智能不仅提高了电子产品的投入成本，而且还推动了支持消费者需求的积极财富效应。”

“沃什主席一直宣扬的人工智能的通货紧缩效应还需要再等一段时间。”

这对于股票来说涉及两个方面：短期利率和长期利率。

在收益率曲线的短端，人工智能导致通胀上升，使利率政策变得复杂化。 通胀越高，美联储提高隔夜贷款利率的压力就越大。 这会抑制经济活动，并可能减缓盈利增长——股票市场的命脉。

Sevens Report Research 的创始人 Tom Essaye 周四告诉我，虽然人工智能的发展不太可能导致持续的通胀，但它确实强化了美联储 9 月会议上一次性加息的理由。

另一方面，通货膨胀往往会推高长期债券收益率，因为当投资者预计通货膨胀会侵蚀其货币价值时，他们会要求更高的回报。 10年期国债收益率目前为4.64%，高于年初的4.15%。

MRB Partners 在周四的一份客户报告中表示，虽然影响长期利率的因素有很多，但投资支出的增加正在帮助提高债券收益率。 该公司预计长期收益率将进一步上升，这可能会给股​​市带来麻烦。

MRB Partners全球策略合伙人菲利普·科尔马(Philip Colmar)在报告中表示，“我们对美国国债的悲观前景最终将给美国股市带来问题。” 他补充说，自 2020 年以来，每次 10 年期国债收益率大幅突破上行，“股市都会经历大幅调整”。
